channel.title: The Brussels Times
channel.description: Latest Brussels posts from The Brussels Times.

item.title: Thousands march against militarisation in Brussels
item.description: The demonstration was organised by dozens of Belgian and European civil society groups under the slogan, “War fever destroys, welfare protects!”

item.title: Police and Child Focus on lookout for missing woman and toddler daughter
item.description: The 34-year-old woman and her daughter were last seen on Marie Curie Square in Anderlecht on Thursday morning.

item.title: Student union organises university blockade in Brussels
item.description: The protest is support of a major trade union protest in Brussels and will start at 9:00 from the Brussels North train station.

item.title: From train stations to public spaces: Brussels seeks closer ties with EU
item.description: “The presence of the European institutions is an opportunity for Brussels, but it is also a responsibility. The people who work and live here must be able to feel at home in our city.”

item.title: Anderlecht asks federal government to fund welfare for people losing unemployment benefits
item.description: Anderlecht’s council approved a motion calling on the federal government to fully fund the subsistence income of people who lose their unemployment benefits.

item.title: Turner exhibition promises to 'dazzle' as it aims to attract Brussels visitors
item.description: “We previously staged the show at the Villa Vauban in Luxembourg where it attracted a record attendance of 24,000. I think we can expect many more than that.”

item.title: National strike on Monday: What disruptions are expected in Brussels?
item.description: Thousands of people are expected to join Monday's national demonstration in Brussels to denounce the social budget cuts of Belgium's federal government.

item.title: Two Belgian shopping streets named among Europe's most expensive
item.description: The two streets, one in Antwerp and one in Brussels, share 41st place in the ranking of Europe's most expensive shopping streets.

item.title: Brussels traffic and public transport disruptions due to Saint-Verhaegen celebrations on Friday
item.description: Thousands of students are expected to take to the streets of Brussels on Friday 20 November for the annual Saint-Verhaegen celebrations.

item.title: New flight path measures fail to reduce aircraft noise over Brussels
item.description: Changes to flight procedures at Brussels Airport introduced in October have failed to significantly reduce noise pollution for Brussels residents.

item.title: Over 10,000 more job seekers in Brussels at risk of relying on public assitance by June
item.description: Brussels Employment and Economy Minister Laurent Hublet said he expects nearly 10,000 more jobseekers to receive social assistance by June 2027.

item.title: Brussels issued no low-emission fines to foreign plates in 2025 and 2026
item.description: Despite issuing 17,717 fines to Belgian vehicles in 2025 and 2026, Brussels issued no low-emission fines to vehicles with foreign plates during this time.

item.title: Brussels fire department responded to 30 incidents due to stormy weather
item.description: The Brussels fire department has responded to 30 weather-related incidents Tuesday evening and night, mainly for flooding.

item.title: Brussels Christmas market celebrates 25 years with Mont des Arts panoramic village
item.description: The organisers and the City of Brussels announced the programme on Tuesday morning, the event will run from 27 November to 3 January.

item.title: Police deploy water cannons in Brussels against student protestors
item.description: The protests, organised by the French-speaking student umbrella group FEF were called in response to rising tuition fees and education cuts.

item.title: Police seek two men linked to attempted murder at Ixelles nighclub
item.description: Police have issued an appeal to identify and trace two suspects linked to an attempted murder at an Avenue Louise nightclub.

item.title: Dott to comply with ban on shared e-scooters in Brussels drug hotspots
item.description: Dott told customers that scooters entering one of the 19 restricted zones across several Brussels municipalities will automatically stop.

item.title: Students to protest in Brussels against rising tuition fees on Tuesday
item.description: The French-speaking student protest on Tuesday will be backed by the trade unions FGTB, CSC, and Flemish-speaking students.

item.title: €50,000 seized following alleged drug deal in Brussels
item.description: The Brussels-Capital/Ixelles police zone said on Monday that the cash, believed to be linked to drug trafficking, was found during a house search.

item.title: 'Losing hope': Flemish couple delays wedding over Molenbeek birth certificate backlog
item.description: Even intervention by the Brussels Ombudsman failed to break the deadlock after several formal complaints.
